key_insight: Combining coarse 3D scene geometry with 2D video references enables generative models to produce spatially consistent, temporally coherent previsualizations quickly — without requiring polished assets or deep 3D expertise.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between imprecise hand-drawn storyboards and demanding full 3D previsualization by enabling fast, expressive video-level prototypes that preserve spatial relationships and camera intent.
method: Use rough 3D scenes (simple geometry + camera paths) as spatial and camera constraints for generation.
Condition a generative video model on 2D reference footage/styles to transfer appearance and motion cues.
Synthesize temporally coherent previsualization frames that respect the 3D layout while enabling rapid iteration.
impact: Makes previsualization accessible and faster for filmmakers and creatives while giving AI/ML practitioners a concrete multimodal conditioning task (3D→2D + temporal consistency) to advance generative video research and evaluation.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: rough 3D scene + camera path + 2D reference video → generative model → previsualization video
Before/after comparison: hand-drawn storyboard vs PrevizWhiz output highlighting improved spatial fidelity
Overlay visuals: camera trajectory and depth/geometry projection on generated frames to show spatial consistency
Iteration timeline: quick edits to 3D scene or reference leading to rapid new previews (speed/efficiency chart)
paper_title: PrevizWhiz: Combining Rough 3D Scenes and 2D Video to Guide Generative Video Previsualization
paper_authors: Erzhen Hu, Frederik Brudy, David Ledo, George Fitzmaurice, Fraser Anderson
